title: Georgian short-term residence permit for owners of real estate worth more than USD 150,000, with their spouse and children

sources.title: Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, art. 15(j): a short-term permit for an alien owning non-agricultural real estate worth over USD 150,000, and their spouse and children
Law No. 863-IIმს-XIმპ of 26 June 2025, art. 1(2)(b) and art. 2(2): the USD 150,000 threshold of art. 15(j) (USD 100,000 before) applies from 1 March 2026
Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, art. 16(1)(f) and (3): extended one year at a time while the alien owns the real estate, up to 12 years
Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, arts. 2(a) and 14(1): residence permits go to aliens, persons who are not citizens of Georgia, staying in Georgia on a lawful ground
Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, art. 14(1) to (1^4): a lawful stay, which excludes asylum seekers, deferred departures, ordinary C visas and art. 10(3^1) entries
Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, art. 18(1) and (4): refusal grounds such as state security, criminal record, false documents, and expulsion proceedings
Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, art. 2(h): a family member is a spouse and a minor child of an alien, among others
Civil Code of Georgia, art. 12(2): a person who has turned 18 is of the age of majority
Civil Code of Georgia, art. 123(3): a period whose last month lacks the start day ends on that month's last day, so a 29 February birthday counts on 28 February

requirements.title: Funds for a Georgian property, not agricultural land, whose market value exceeds USD 150,000 (in GEL)
Not a citizen of Georgia: residence permits are only for aliens

assessments.title: Ownership of the property registered under Georgian law, its value set by a certified assessor of an accredited body; the permit ends if the ownership ends
In Georgia on a lawful ground when applying: not as an asylum seeker, on a deferred obligation to leave, on an ordinary C visa or under art. 10(3^1) (entry on another country's visa or permit)
None of the refusal grounds: a security risk, certain criminal records or prosecutions, a disease dangerous to the public, false documents or data, expulsion proceedings

dependents.title: Children under 18; art. 15(j) gives no age, but the law's family member is a minor child, so a child of 18 or more: possible

costs.title: Real estate in Georgia, not agricultural land, worth more than USD 150,000
